ChatGPT said:ChatGPT

For Stacko, I recommend building the Instagram page as a product showroom, not a traditional company page.

When someone visits for the first time, they should understand three things within a few seconds:

  1. What is Stacko?

  2. What problem does it solve?

  3. How can I see it working?

Since this is a new page, we won't depend on testimonials or customer reviews. Instead, we'll use product demos, clear explanations, interface previews, and educational content to build trust.

Profile image: Use the Stacko icon only, without the full tagline. It needs to remain recognizable at a small size.

POST 02 — Multiple warehouses. One view.

Visual headline: One map. All your warehouses.

Managing stock across different locations can make it difficult to see the complete picture.

Stacko brings your warehouse locations and stock movements into one visual view.

Know where your inventory is and follow its movement.

Your stock. Always in sight.

#Stacko #WarehouseManagement #InventoryVisibility #StockControl

POST 03 — The inventory problem

Visual headline: Can you answer these three questions?

Where is this item?

Which warehouse has it?

Is the incoming shipment received yet?

When inventory information is spread across different files and systems, getting clear answers becomes harder.

Stacko is designed to bring these operations into one place.

#Stacko #InventoryProblems #StockManagement #BusinessOperations

POST 04 — Dashboard preview

Visual headline: Your inventory, organized in one place.

An inventory system should help you understand your operations, not make them more complicated.

With Stacko, explore your stock information, warehouse activity, and inventory movements through one dashboard.

Take a closer look at the product.

#Stacko #InventoryDashboard #WarehouseSoftware #InventoryManagement

POST 05 — Product demo

Visual headline: See Stacko in action.

Enough talking about inventory management. Let's see it.

In this demo, we'll walk through the Stacko interface and show how warehouse information and stock movements can be viewed.

This is a look at the product itself.

Watch the demo and explore Stacko.

#Stacko #ProductDemo #InventorySoftware #WarehouseManagement

POST 06 — Shipment visibility

Visual headline: From shipment to warehouse.

An incoming shipment is an important part of your inventory operations.

But knowing that goods are on their way is not the same as knowing they have arrived and been received.

Stacko helps you follow shipment progress and keep the receiving process visible.

#Stacko #ShipmentTracking #InventoryManagement #SupplyChain

POST 07 — Purchased doesn't mean received

Visual headline: Purchased ≠ Available Stock

A purchase order tells you what you've ordered.

It doesn't automatically mean the goods are already available in your warehouse.

Receiving is a separate step, and keeping these stages clear matters.

Understand the difference. Keep your inventory information accurate.

#Stacko #InventoryTips #PurchaseOrders #WarehouseManagement

POST 08 — Warehouse operations

Visual headline: Every movement matters.

Moving products between warehouses is part of daily inventory operations.

But every movement needs to be recorded and followed.

Stacko helps make warehouse-to-warehouse movements easier to follow through a centralized view.

#Stacko #WarehouseTransfers #StockMovements #InventoryControl

POST 09 — Explore Stacko

Visual headline: Ready to see your stock differently?

Your warehouses. Your inventory. Your movements.

Bring your inventory operations into one visual experience with Stacko.

Visit our website to learn more and explore the product.

5. Instagram Story Highlights

Highlights should work like the navigation menu of your website.

I recommend starting with these six:

Start Here

What is Stacko?

Demo

Product walkthroughs

Features

What Stacko does

Inventory Tips

Helpful explanations

Common questions

Get in touch

What to put inside each highlight:

  • Start Here: Welcome, what Stacko is, who it is for, the main problem it addresses.

  • Demo: Short screen recordings showing actual product workflows.

  • Features: Warehouse map, stock movements, shipment tracking, receiving.

  • Inventory Tips: Purchase order vs received stock, transfers, stock accuracy.

  • FAQ: What is Stacko? Who is it for? How does it work? How can I request a demo?

  • Contact: Website, business email, and a clear contact invitation.

Only add features that are currently working and demonstrable to the relevant highlights.

6. The three pinned posts

Instagram allows you to pin three posts at the top of the profile. These are your most important posts.

PIN 1 — What is Stacko?

Introduce the product, target audience, and main value proposition.

PIN 2 — Product Demo

Your strongest demo video. Let visitors see the real product immediately.

PIN 3 — How Stacko Works

Explain the core workflow with a simple visual example.

7. What a new visitor should experience

This is the visitor journey I want the page to create:

  1. Profile photo and bio

    Immediately understand that Stacko is an inventory management product.

  2. Pinned introduction

    Understand the problem Stacko is designed to solve.

  3. Pinned product demo

    See the actual interface, not just marketing promises.

  4. Highlights

    Explore features, learn useful concepts, and find answers.

  5. Post grid

    Discover product details, educational content, and real workflows.

  6. Call to action

    Visit the website or contact Stacko to learn more or request a demo.

8. What not to publish yet

Because Stacko is a new product page:

  • Don't create fake testimonials.

  • Don't use invented customer success stories.

  • Don't publish customer logos without permission.

  • Don't claim specific business results without evidence.

  • Don't make every post a sales advertisement.

  • Don't show conceptual features as if they're already available.

Instead, let the product itself be your proof. Screen recordings, real interface details, and clear demonstrations can build credibility without testimonials.

10. The next design stage

The strategy is ready. The next step is to turn it into a consistent visual system.

I recommend creating these actual assets:

  • Instagram profile picture.

  • Six highlight covers.

  • Three pinned-post designs.

  • Nine launch-post designs.

  • Reel cover templates.

  • Carousel templates.

  • Story templates.

One important decision before creating the visuals: I would use the actual Stacko dashboard and map screenshots in the designs rather than generate fake software interfaces. That way, the Instagram page accurately represents the product.

I can build the visual direction around the Stacko brand kit, with consistent layouts and editable text areas, so the whole profile looks like one professionally designed product launch.
